test.title: Should children be paid for chores?

texts.title: Should children be paid for chores?

paragraphs.text: Paying children for household jobs is common, and many parents defend it as a way to teach the value of money. I understand the reasoning, but I think it sends the wrong message about what it means to be part of a family.

Some tasks, such as keeping one’s own room tidy or clearing the table after dinner, are simply what everyone in a household does. If children are paid for these, they may reasonably ask why they should help at all when they do not need the money.

That said, I see nothing wrong with paying for jobs that go beyond normal family duties, such as washing the car or helping a neighbour with their garden. These can teach children that effort can be exchanged for income.

Pocket money can also be given without any link to chores. A regular weekly amount allows children to practise saving and making choices, and in my experience it is at least as effective at teaching the value of money.

document.title: Should children be paid for chores?

items.prompt: The writer understands why some parents pay their children for chores.

explanation.en: “I understand the reasoning” — the writer understands the parents’ argument, even though he disagrees with the conclusion → YES.
explanation.kk: «I understand the reasoning» — автор ата-аналардың дәлелін түсінеді, бірақ қорытындысымен келіспейді → YES.
explanation.ru: «I understand the reasoning» — автор понимает довод родителей, хотя с выводом не согласен → YES.

items.quote: are simply what everyone in a household does
items.prompt: The writer thinks children should be paid for keeping their own rooms tidy.

explanation.en: Tidying one’s own room is “what everyone in a household does”, and the writer does not want it paid for → NO.
explanation.kk: Өз бөлмесін жинау — «what everyone in a household does», автор бұл үшін ақы төлеуді ұсынбайды → NO.
explanation.ru: Уборка своей комнаты — это то, «what everyone in a household does», и платить за это автор не предлагает → NO.

items.quote: they may reasonably ask why they should help at all
items.prompt: The writer believes most children would refuse to help without payment.

explanation.en: The writer says children “may reasonably ask” why they should help. He never claims most would refuse → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.kk: Автор балалар «may reasonably ask» — не үшін көмектесу керек деп сұрауы мүмкін дейді. Балалардың көбі бас тартады деп айтпайды → NOT GIVEN.
explanation.ru: Автор допускает, что дети «may reasonably ask», зачем помогать. Откажется ли большинство детей, он не утверждает → NOT GIVEN.

items.quote: I see nothing wrong with paying for jobs that go beyond normal family duties
items.prompt: The writer is against paying children for any kind of work.

explanation.en: “I see nothing wrong with paying for jobs that go beyond normal family duties” — extra jobs can be paid. “Any kind of work” is an over-generalisation → NO.
explanation.kk: «I see nothing wrong with paying for jobs that go beyond normal family duties» — қосымша жұмыс үшін төлеуге болады. «Any kind of work» — жалпылау → NO.
explanation.ru: «I see nothing wrong with paying for jobs that go beyond normal family duties» — за дополнительную работу платить можно. «Any kind of work» — обобщение → NO.

items.quote: it is at least as effective at teaching the value of money
items.prompt: The writer believes regular pocket money can teach children the value of money.

explanation.en: In the writer’s experience, regular pocket money is “at least as effective at teaching the value of money” as paying for chores → YES.
explanation.kk: Автордың тәжірибесінше, тұрақты қалтақаржы «at least as effective at teaching the value of money» — ақшаның құнын жұмыс ақысынан кем үйретпейді → YES.
explanation.ru: По опыту автора, регулярные карманные деньги «at least as effective at teaching the value of money» — учат ценности денег не хуже платы за работу → YES.

groups.instruction: Questions 1–5. Look at the text. Do the following statements agree with the views of the writer? Write YES if the statement agrees with the views of the writer, NO if the statement contradicts the views of the writer, or NOT GIVEN if it is impossible to say what the writer thinks about this.
